clinical_knowledge.topic: Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe progressive motor deficit.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: right shoulder pain when painting ceilings and pain when sleeping on that side

55M house painter reports 3 months of aching pain in his right shoulder. Pain is worst when reaching overhead to paint or when sleeping directly on his right side.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination. Evaluate for pertinent signs.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: Perform Neer and Hawkins impingement maneuvers. Recommend physical therapy focusing on scapular stabilization and rotator cuff strengthening. Consider a clinician-performed subacromial corticosteroid injection only after diagnostic reassessment and an inadequate response to conservative care. Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling.

must_ask.say: Did the shoulder pain start after a lot of overhead reaching or activity, like painting?
Is the pain worst in a specific range when you lift your arm, like between shoulder and ear height?

must_ask.objective: Night pain when lying on shoulder
must_ask.say: Does the pain wake you up at night, especially when lying on that shoulder?
Do you feel true weakness lifting your arm, or is it mainly pain stopping you?
Have you tried any physical therapy, rest, or injections, and what activities are you hoping to get back to?

history.answer: My right shoulder has been hurting for the past three months, especially when I reach up to paint ceilings or lie on that side at night.
It is just my right shoulder; no other joints in my arms, neck, or legs hurt.
It started gradually about three months ago and has been slowly getting more bothersome.
It is a dull, deep ache over the top and outside of the shoulder, usually around a 4 or 5 out of 10, but it shoots up to a 7 when I reach up high.
No, there is no swelling, warmth, or redness around the shoulder.
I feel a little stiff when I first wake up because I tossed and turned, but it loosens up within ten minutes once I start moving around.
Reaching overhead, lifting my arm out to the side, and sleeping directly on my right side make it worse; resting my arm at my side helps.
It hurts most when my arm is halfway up, around shoulder level, but if I push through past the top it does not hurt quite as much.
Whenever I roll onto my right shoulder during the night, the ache wakes me up and I have to shift over.
I can still do my daily chores, but reaching up to paint high walls and ceilings has become almost impossible without pain.
My arm still feels strong, but sometimes I drop it slightly simply because the pain bites when I hold it out.
No, I have not had any fevers or chills.
No, there was no sudden fall, pop, or trauma; it just built up from years of painting and overhead work.
No, I have never had shoulder trouble or pain like this before.
No, I have not felt tired, run-down, or lost any weight.
No rashes, mouth sores, hair loss, or dry eyes at all.
No back stiffness, heel pain, or swollen fingers or toes.
No, I have not had diarrhea, burning with urination, or any colds recently.
No, I do not drink much, I eat normally, and I am not taking water pills.
No, I have never taken steroid pills, had joint injections, or had any joint surgery.
I am happily married for twenty-five years with only my wife; no other partners.
I have high blood pressure, which was diagnosed about four years ago.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once a day for my blood pressure, and I take ibuprofen once in a while when the shoulder aches.
I do not have any allergies to medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I might have one beer on a Saturday evening, but that is about it.
I work full-time as an interior house painter and live with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure, but there is no history of rheumatoid arthritis or other joint conditions in my family.
I think it might be rotator cuff tendinitis or wear-and-tear from all the overhead rolling and brushing I do.
I am really worried that I might need surgery, because if I cannot work with my arm, I cannot earn a living.
I was hoping to try physical therapy and maybe get a cortisone shot so I can keep working without severe pain.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Well-developed, comfortable male sitting upright, guarding the right shoulder slightly with movement.
Full cervical active range of motion without midline tenderness or pain reproduction during Spurling's test.

Right shoulder shows tenderness over the anterior-lateral acromion and greater tuberosity, full passive motion, painful active abduction arc between 70 and 120 degrees, and positive Neer and Hawkins impingement tests.
Full 5/5 strength in bilateral upper extremities, with mild breakaway weakness on right supraspinatus empty-can and resisted external rotation due to shoulder pain.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation throughout the C5 through T1 dermatomes bilaterally.
Biceps, brachioradialis, and triceps deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
No rashes, psoriatic plaques, tophi, or nail changes on inspection.
